captured.note: peet.ws prints the PRIORITY section as 0, while the HEADERS frame itself arrived with the Priority flag (weight 256, exclusive, depends_on 0), which fingerproxy shows as 1:1:0:256

tls.note: two samples gave different extension orders for the same set — the shuffling is confirmed by measurement. The set matched chrome-150-macos and the JA4 matched chrome-151-windows, so the profile is written as a delta

accept_encoding.HEAD: gzip, deflate, br, zstd, sdch
accept_encoding.note: sdch is a Yandex Browser tell; Chromium dropped it. The rule is about the method rather than the body: a POST with an empty body also goes without sdch, while a PUT with a body carries it

headers.note: the HTTP/1.1 order and case, the fetch set and the WebSocket handshake matched Chrome's templates name for name — the sections are inherited from chrome-151-windows deliberately, not by default

not_measured: HTTP/3 and QUIC. Could not be captured: the browser rejects the stand's certificate specifically over QUIC (TLS alert 46, certificate unknown), while the same certificate passes over TCP. Chromium demands a chain to a publicly known root for QUIC, and there is no --ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list on Android. The http3 and quic sections are inherited from chrome-151-windows

client_hints.requested_via: Accept-CH in the stand's response, measured over USB
client_hints.note: Yandex's full version is its own rather than Chromium's, unlike Chrome where sec-ch-ua-full-version equals the browser version. The order of the cluster with the hints matched Chrome 152

devices.measured: Pixel 7 / Android 17 / arm_64 — taken from the phone
devices.plausible: the other model-and-version pairs in the profile were not checked on devices
devices.note: Yandex puts the device in the User-Agent as well, so it is substituted in both places: the string and the hints have to agree
